trigger.observed: The compiler retirement fix alone did not prevent a 900-second unchanged closure timeout on macOS. Repeated uncaptured weak reads still shaded their targets during propagation.

reviewed_invariants: The only runtime change is conditional omission of Root_Barrier for uncaptured scalar writes. Captured slots retain the original Root_Barrier before cache publication and Store_Cell afterward; heap, code, operation-packet and native result barriers are unchanged.

Root_Barrier previously acted only during Propagating. Atomic is indivisible: Trace_Roots, gray-again thread transfer, Propagate_All and ephemeron convergence precede weak-value clearing. The finalizer-root wave and another convergence precede the second weak clearing pass.

Every propagated thread enters Gray_Again during propagation. Reachable suspended Lua-owned threads are therefore rescanned even when they are absent from the active-root family. Main, host-owned, running and normal contexts remain explicit roots.

A retained scalar value is discovered from its actual live interval at atomic; a consumed value overwritten before atomic adds no heap edge. Stacks.Trace continues to validate and visit the exact ordered interval union, including detached public resume windows and borrowed warning prefixes.

Stacks.Write and captured-cell stores perform no allocation. Canonical fixed/open result publication reserves storage before nonallocating slot writes and top publication; frame opening roots callee/arguments before reserve and copies; Foreign.Push reserves before its nonallocating write followed by Publish_Top.

Sweep behavior is unchanged because the previous root barrier did not run during sweeping. New allocations retain their current-white semantics. Generational minors are indivisible and old thread stacks stay remembered; heap old-to-young barriers are unchanged.

The four private phase cases verify transient and retained main/suspended slots. Suspended cases explicitly reach Revisit_Gray while propagation is unfinished; saved immutable serials and weak slots verify actual reclamation or survival without dereferencing freed objects.

The public Lua regression retains 1000 tables, repeatedly consumes weak reads and performs 2000 small manual collection steps. It reproduces the defect with the previous compiler fix already present, so the new test isolates propagation shading rather than host timing.
